Property & Land Law Practice Guide

Legal Due Diligence Checklist for Buying Land and Property in Nepal

📅 Published: 2025-04-20
🔄 Updated: 2025-10-01
⏱ 10 min read
🔍 Review: Senior Advocate Lead Counsel, Supreme Court Bar Association
Direct Legal Answer & Overview

Legal due diligence for buying land in Nepal requires verifying ten critical factors: 1) Malpot Shrestha title ledger ownership; 2) Survey Office (Napi) boundary and road access alignment; 3) Rokka search confirming absence of bank mortgage or court freezes; 4) Co-heir consent if property is unpartitioned ancestral land; 5) Non-Guthi land classification; 6) Absence of tenant rights (Mohi); 7) High-voltage transmission line, river-bank, or highway setback restrictions; 8) Up-to-date municipal tax payments; 9) Clear Byna-patra agreement terms; and 10) Physical on-site neighborhood inquiry.

Key Practical Takeaways

  • Never pay substantial earnest money (Byna) before completing title due diligence.
  • Verify municipal road setbacks and high-voltage transmission easements.
  • Confirm that ancestral land is not sold without adult co-heir written consent.

Purchasing real estate in Nepal is typically the largest financial investment a family or enterprise ever undertakes. Yet, buyers frequently hand over millions of rupees in earnest money (Byna) without verifying whether the seller possesses clean, unencumbered title. A structured 10-point legal due diligence audit eliminates fatal transactional pitfalls.

1. The 10-Point Land Due Diligence Audit

  1. Title Chain Verification: Inspect the historical deed chain (Shrestha) for at least the past 20 years to confirm lawful origin (sale, partition, or gift).
  2. Rokka Encumbrance Status: Confirm no commercial bank mortgages, tax liens, or court freezes exist on the plot.
  3. Mohi (Tenancy Rights) Check: Under the Land Act 2021, if a tenant farmer (Mohi) is registered on the land, they legally own 50% of the land value upon partition. Confirm the Shrestha reads 'Mohi Nabhayeko' (No tenant).
  4. Guthi Classification: Verify the land is Raikar (private freehold) and not Rajguthi, which cannot be freely alienated without Guthi Sansthan approvals.
  5. Cadastral Map vs. Ground Reality: Ensure the plot mapped on the Napi Blue Print matches physical boundaries, access roads, and adjoining properties.
  6. Road Access & Setback Compliance: Verify whether access roads meet municipal building bylaws (commonly 6 to 8 meters minimum in urban zones) and ensure no river setback (Nadi Kinar Mapdanda) impacts buildability.
  7. High-Voltage Transmission Lines: Land underneath high-tension power lines carries strict building bans under electricity regulations.
  8. Ancestral Consent (Anshiyar Hak): If the seller acquired land via inheritance, confirm whether adult children and spouse consent, preventing future partition challenges.
  9. Tax & Dues Clearance: Verify that local municipal land taxes (Malpot Tiro) are fully paid up to the current fiscal year.
  10. On-Site Neighborhood Inquiry: Conduct discrete inquiries with adjoining plot owners to ensure no boundary conflicts or unrecorded easement disputes exist.

Statutory Citations & Governing Nepal Legislation

Statute / Act Section / Rule Legal Significance
Land Act 2021 Chapter 7 (Tenancy Rights / Mohi) Restrictions on buying land encumbered by protected agricultural tenants.
Muluki Civil Code 2074 Chapter on Property and Sales Validity of property sale contracts and warranties of title.

Documentary Checklist for this Procedure

  • ✔ Lalpurja copy and Shrestha search certificate
  • ✔ Cadastral Blue Print and Trace map from Napi Karyalaya
  • ✔ Municipal Road Access Certificate (Sadak Pramanikaran)
  • ✔ Municipal property tax clearance receipt (Tiro Tireko Rasid)

Frequently Asked Questions on this Topic

What should a buyer include in an earnest money agreement (Byna-patra)?

The Byna-patra should specify: exact plot number and area, total agreed price, payment schedule, deadline for Malpot transfer, and an explicit clause that earnest money must be fully refunded if legal due diligence uncovers title defects or bank encumbrances.
